data.hypothesis: Starting from the substantially faster measured warp-per-target candidate, staging source fields once per CTA may reduce repeated global source loads across its eight warps. Shared-memory staging and barriers could also add overhead, so this full composition requires fresh measurement.
data.notes: T2 (3001b0f6ac854db4) is the justified starting program: it was valid and correct at a reported mean of 0.0001166883 s, versus 0.0009947159 s for valid, correct T1 (5d078c6a6edd41aa). Those are search measurements, not independent confirmation. This proposal combines T1's 2048-source, 32 KiB shared tile with T2's warp-per-target traversal, lane-strided accumulation, rsqrtf interaction, and shuffle reduction. It is an unmeasured composition; retain the better input if the controller's result regresses.
transformations: Preserved T2's one-target-per-warp ownership, lane-strided source traversal, warp shuffle reduction, rsqrtf inverse-distance-cubed calculation, and lane-zero complete-state output.
Integrated T1's four dynamic shared-memory arrays for source x, y, z, and mass, staging up to 2048 source particles per tile for reuse across CTA warps.
Kept all block threads participating in both barriers, including inactive target-tail warps; source tile loads and interactions are bounded by valid counts.
Set block=256, items_per_block=8 (one target per warp), and shared_memory_bytes=32768.
